IC.IC1: Eligible patients must meet the following criteria to be enrolled in the study:

IC2.IC2.1: 1. Newly diagnosed, stage IV squamous cell lung cancer. This includes patients who present with disseminated metastases, and those with a malignant pleural
IC2.IC2.2: or pericardial effusion (i.e., formerly stage IIIB in the 6th TNM staging system).

IC3.IC3.1: 2. Patients who have received prior adjuvant therapy for early-stage lung cancer
IC3.IC3.2: are eligible if at least 12 months have elapsed from that treatment.

IC4.IC4.2: confirmed squamous cell bronchogenic carcinoma. Patients whose tumors contain mixed non-small cell histologies
IC4.IC4.3: are eligible, as long as squamous carcinoma is the predominant histology. Mixed tumors with
IC4.IC4.4: small cell anaplastic elements are not eligible. Cytologic specimens obtained by brushings, washings, or needle aspiration of the defined lesion are acceptable.

IC5.IC5.2: as definitive therapy for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer are eligible, as long as the recurrence is outside the original radiation therapy port. Radiation therapy must have been completed >4 weeks prior to the initiation of study treatment. Patients who have received
IC5.IC5.3: chemo/radiation for locally advanced NSCLC are not eligible. Patients who have received palliative radiation therapy
IC5.IC5.4: for symptomatic metastases must have completed treatment >14 days prior the initiation of the study treatment.

IC.IC10: Hemoglobin >9 g/dL (Note: Patients may be transfused or receive erythropoietin to maintain or exceed this level).

IC12.IC12.3: or ≤5 times the upper limit of normal with liver involvement.

IC13.IC13.2: <2.0 mg/dL, or creatinine clearance >40 mL/min (as calculated by the Cockcroft-Gault method.

IC.IC14: 8. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test performed within 7 days prior to start of treatment. Women of childbearing potential or men with partners of childbearing potential must use effective birth control measures during treatment and at least 6 months after the last dose of the study treatment. If a woman becomes pregnant or suspects she is pregnant while participating in this study, she must agree to inform her treating physician immediately. Sexually active men must agree to use a medically acceptable form of birth control during treatment and at least 6 months after the last dose. If a female partner becomes pregnant during the course of the study the treating physician should be informed immediately.
IC.IC16: 10. Ability to understand the nature of this study, give written informed consent, and comply with study requirements.
IC.IC17: 11. Patients entering this study must be willing to provide tissue from a previous tumor biopsy (if available) for correlative testing. An exception to this is when the national/local regulations prohibits some of the key activities of this research like the export of samples to third countries, storage of coded samples or global gene expression profiling without a pre-specified list of target genes. If tissue is not available, a patient will still be eligible for enrollment into the study.
